questions.question: We usually have ___ lunch at noon.
questions.explanation: Names of meals generally take no article when referring to routine meals.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Names of languages generally do not take an article.

questions.question: My favourite subject is ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: Names of academic subjects generally take no article.

questions.question: They invited us to ___ dinner yesterday.
questions.explanation: The name of a meal normally takes no article when used in its ordinary sense.

questions.question: Which sentence uses an article incorrectly?
questions.explanation: Language names generally take no article. The correct sentence is 'He understands Hindi.'

questions.question: ___ Chemistry is an interesting subject.
questions.explanation: Academic subject names such as chemistry generally take no article.

questions.question: We had ___ wonderful dinner at a restaurant.
questions.explanation: When a meal is described with an adjective, it can take an indefinite article: 'a wonderful dinner'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The French is spoken in France.
A French is spoken in France.
An French is spoken in France.
questions.explanation: The name of a language used in its ordinary sense takes no article.

questions.question: He is studying ___ history at college.
questions.explanation: Academic subjects generally take no article when used as fields of study.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: We had a breakfast at 7 a.m.
We had an breakfast at 7 a.m.
We had the breakfast in general at 7 a.m.
questions.explanation: Breakfast in its ordinary sense generally takes no article.

questions.question: ___ Japanese is difficult for some learners.
questions.explanation: Language names generally do not take articles.

questions.question: She gave me ___ early breakfast before the journey.
questions.explanation: An adjective describing a meal can make it a particular countable occasion. 'Early' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The biology is my favourite subject.
A biology is my favourite subject.
An biology is my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Names of academic subjects generally take no article.

questions.question: They usually have ___ tea at 5 p.m.
questions.explanation: Tea as a meal or routine refreshment generally takes no article.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Names of languages generally do not take an article.

questions.question: ___ Economics helps us understand how resources are allocated.
questions.explanation: Economics is the name of an academic subject and normally takes no article.
